items.title: France : 2025, la quatrième année la plus chaude jamais enregistrée
items.description: L’année 2025 a été la quatrième année la plus chaude jamais enregistrée en France, selon le premier bilan annuel des impacts du changement climatique publié par le ministère de la Transition écologique. Cette année témoigne de l’accélération du changement climatique dans le pays, avec notamment deux vagues de chaleur majeures ayant touché près de 80 % de la population et des restrictions d’usage de l’eau mises en place dans 78 départements, ressort-il de ce bilan. Par ailleurs, plus de 30.500 hectares ont été ravagés par des feux de forêt, tandis que le coût des événements naturels a été estimé à 5,2 milliards d’euros. Face à cette situation, le ministère souligne la nécessité de poursuivre les efforts de réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, conformément à la Stratégie nationale bas-carbone, qui fixe la trajectoire de la France vers la neutralité carbone à l’horizon 2050. Le bilan dresse un état des lieux des conséquences déjà observables du dérèglement climatique en France et sera actualisé chaque année afin de suivre l’évolution de ces impacts et de contribuer à l’élaboration des politiques publiques. Le ministère rappelle ainsi que l’adaptation au changement climatique constitue désormais un impératif complémentaire à la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre The post France : 2025, la quatrième année la plus chaude jamais enregistrée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: I got paid $5,000 to move from Portland to a place I’d never heard of
items.description: When Brianna Beyrouti looks back on her former life in Portland, Oregon, she says she was financially “drowning”. “I was absolutely living paycheque to paycheque. Every time the smallest thing came up, it was like ‘Oh, gosh, the kids need shoes, how am I going to afford that?’ As a single parent, everything falls on my shoulders.” Last year, Brianna left Portland and its metropolitan population of 2.5 million people. She and her two children moved 2,000 miles east to Muncie, Indiana, a small city with 65,000 people, a university and lots of open space, taking advantage of a scheme that contributed $5,000 towards the cost of the move to boost population growth. The relocation has been a revelation for her finances. She continues to work remotely for the same bank, so her annual salary of $107,000 (£79,000) is unchanged, but she has been able to buy a home for the first time. And her mortgage is less than what she used to pay in rent. In Portland she was paying rent of $1,290 a month for an apartment, while the combined cost of her mortgage, home insurance and property tax for her detached home in Muncie is $1,100. Add the fact that state income tax is lower in Indiana, and that her car insurance and energy bills have also fallen, and Brianna says she is $600 a month better off. “I’m able to live my life more than I was before,” she says. “When my kids want something, I’m much more inclined to say yes. My quality of life has increased dramatically.” Cash incentive Brianna and her children swapped Portland for Muncie Brianna is not alone in swapping a big city for a smaller one. As the high cost of living continues to bite in the US, many of the biggest cities are seeing their populations fall, as people leave in search of cheaper property. A 2025 report from the National Association of Realtors found that for people moving to a different state, affordability was their primary reason. As a result, big cities from the likes of New York and Los Angeles to Portland, Oregon have seen a dip in their populations in recent years, further fuelled by the greatly increased acceptance of remote working since the Covid-19 pandemic. By contrast, some small towns and cities across the US, such as Muncie, are seeing their populations rise after decades of decline. The number of people who live in Muncie hit 65,466 last year, official figures showed. This is up from 65,194 in 2020, but still way down on its population of 71,828 in 1990. Free cinema tickets and wine To help it stand out from the crowd, and encourage remote workers to move there from outsideIndiana, Muncie’s local council offers them $5,000 in cash to cover their relocation costs. It does this via a website called MakeMyMove, which lists several such relocation support schemes offered by similar small cities and towns across the US. These pay MakeMyMove a subscription fee. Other incentives locations offer potential new residents are complementary cinema tickets, restaurant vouchers, and even free bottles of wine. Brianna and her children are one of around 100 families to have moved to Muncie through the MakeMyMove programme. She says she hadn’t heard of the city before. Across the US, MakeMyMove says it helped 1,000 people relocate last year and is on track to increase that to 1,500 in 2026. Moving to smalltown America has allowed Elena Chrysostomou to buy a home Scientist Elena Chrysostomou also used a relocation support scheme to swap a big city for smalltown US. In 2024 she relocated from San Diego, California, to Jacksonville, a town of 17,700 people in rural Illinois. The move was backed by the Jacksonville Regional Economic Development Corporation (JREDC), which gave her $5,000 in cash, plus a “quality of life package” worth $4,000 that includes free gym memberships and golf passes. The JREDC says that while the region is “already a great place to live”, the support scheme helps to “sweeten the deal”. Elena was spending $3,000 on rent for a one-bedroom apartment in San Diego, but she now owns a three-bedroom home with a mortgage of $1,868. At the same time, her salary has gone up 22% after she changed jobs, and her commute has gone down from a 15-minute drive to one of just one minute. “I never thought that I’d be able to afford a house on my own, I always thought I’d need a partner, and even then, in San Diego, it would be so tough,” she says. “It’s just more freeing. There’s more security and independence.” While both she and Brianna have no regrets, they do admit to some drawbacks to their new lives. These include the narrower range of activities and restaurant choices, leaving behind friends and family, and for Brianna the difficulty of settling her children into new schools. And while in Portland Brianna enjoyed walking to parks and shops, she now relies on her car to get anywhere. But overall she says she is thrilled. “I have the biggest savings I’ve ever had in my life, and I’m a homeowner, and I can do things with my kids – we actually went on vacation for the first time in my youngest’s life.”

items.title: RDC: Felix Tshisekedi prépare son monologue exclusif!
items.description: Alors que la République démocratique du Congo en pleine guerre, subit de plein fouet un retour dévastateur d’Ebola sous la forme d’une nouvelle souche, le Bundibugyo, déclarée en mai 2026 et qui a déjà fait au moins 3300 morts pour plus de 6 800 cas recensés, le président Félix Tshisekedi, lui, s’est invité sur d’autres fronts. Une nouvelle constitution qui pourrait bien lui ouvrir la voie d’un troisième mandat et l’organisation d’un dialogue national, donc en principe inclusif, constituent les nouvelles priorités du chef de l’Etat congolais. Mais, dans sa volonté officiellement affichée de recherche de la paix dans son pays, le président de la RD Congo ne va-t-il pas plutôt vers un effritement total de la cohésion nationale? Sauf que cette interrogation ne se pose absolument pas pour le président de la république qui vient de profiter de la paisible journée dominicale du 13 septembre 2026, pour signer l’ordonnance créant le comité en charge des préparatifs de ce raout national. Certes, les dates de ce qui pourrait n’être qu’un leurre de plus, dans la quête de la paix, ne sont pas encore fixées, mais le dialogue sera contenu, en principe, dans une période de trois mois. Si dans une patrie écartelée par des querelles intestines, toute initiative née dans le but d’amener ses enfants à se parler est louable, et même noble, il n’en demeure pas moins que l’action doit être guidée par l’objectivité, et surtout la sincérité. Ce qui n’est visiblement pas le cas pour l’instant, au vu des premiers pas de l’instance en préparation. Au lieu d’un arbre à palabre sous lequel toutes les parties auront leur mot à dire afin de crever l’abcès pour de bon, et provoquer une catharsis, le risque est grand que la rencontre se transforme en un gigantesque banquet auquel prendront part des convives qui acclameront des décisions qui seront aussitôt rejetées par les vrais acteurs qui eux, risquent d’être écartés par un pouvoir expert en diversion. Comme le résument et le dénoncent déjà les principaux partis de l’opposition, et certaines organisations de la société civile, Félix Tshisekedi qui détient tous les rouages de l’organisation placée sous son contrôle, ne sera, ni plus, ni moins que juge et partie. En tout cas, si tant est, que le président de la république aspire réellement à la cohésion nationale et croit encore à la démocratie, dans l’intérêt de populations prises entre les feux nourris, au propre comme au figuré, de l’AFC/M23 et l’appétit boulimique d’Ebola, il doit abandonner son projet de 3e mandat qui est à la base de toutes ses manœuvres politiques actuelles. Et il est encore temps pour lui de sortir de son obstination suicidaire de règne sans partage. Il n’est jamais tard pour bien faire, surtout que l’architecture du dialogue n’a pas encore une forme définitive. En dehors de la durée, ni les noms du président, ni ceux des participants, encore moins les dates d’ouverture et de clôture du fameux dialogue, ne sont connus. Questions: qui, mieux que tous les opposants politiques de Felix Tshisekedi, eux qui sont les véritables protagonistes de la vie politique, et l’AFC/M23, ennemi juré des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) dans le Kivu, ont leur place autour de la table des débats? Félix Tshisekedi se rappelle-t-il encore qu’il est opposant, et surtout fils du célèbre opposant Etienne Tshisekedi, pour qui l’alternance constitutionnelle constituait l’essence du combat politique? En tout cas, Felix Tshisekedi, en bon gentleman, peut encore sortir des rails de son monologue exclusif pour emprunter les voies d’un véritable dialogue inclusif, gage d’un retour de la paix durable en RD Congo. Par Wakat Séra L’article RDC: Felix Tshisekedi prépare son monologue exclusif! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: ‘The Flood is the Point’
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Donald Trump loves a deal, even if, at times, it’s just the idea of a deal. The president’s trade dispute with Canada continues to drive one of America’s closest allies into a closer relationship with its chief competition. Although Trump is insisting that “Canada wants to make a deal very badly,” there is very little evidence that’s true, as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney—enjoying broad national approval for his combative response to the American leader—looks to strengthen its alliances in Europe and Asia. Meanwhile, AI leaders are publicly calling for a slowdown. That was the gist of the message delivered by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei this weekend in an essay warning that the technological advances of AI are outpacing the ability to ensure that they are safe. His concerns were echoed by some of the biggest names in tech—OpenAI leader Sam Altman and Elon Musk. But the president saw something else in their warnings: “There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China,” Trump wrote on his social-media site this morning. This week on Radio Atlantic , my colleagues Ashley Parker and Tom Nichols join me to discuss the president’s trade war with Canada, the Trump-centric Republican midterm convention in Dallas, and whether an aging Congress can regulate AI. The following is a transcript of the episode: Ashley Parker: To be somewhat fair to Trump, or to anyone, is that this is just fundamentally incredibly complex. If you’ve ever watched these members of Congress—which is basically a gerontocracy—try to get to the bottom of Snapchat or Instagram or social media with teens, right, it’s like they’re speaking a foreign language, and those are table stakes, right? AI is a million times more complicated than posting a problematic video on YouTube or Instagram. Adam Harris: This is Radio Atlantic . I’m Adam Harris. Congress is back on Capitol Hill for the last time before the midterm elections, and they have a lot to think about—the burgeoning trade war with Canada and warnings from tech CEOs about the dangers of unregulated AI, among other things. And when those lawmakers return to the campaign trail for the final stretch, the ones in competitive districts may have some company—members of the president’s Cabinet. With me to discuss the news of the week are my colleagues Ashley Parker and Tom Nichols. Let’s get to questions. Welcome to the show. Parker: Thanks for having us. Tom Nichols: Thanks, Adam. Harris: Ashley, I want to start with you because you had a story that ran recently about something that people I think have become a little bit desensitized to, and that’s the potential violations of the Hatch Act, which limits the partisan political activities of federal employees. You and our colleague Michael Scherer reported on a competition among the Cabinet secretaries to travel to competitive electoral districts. Can you sort of walk us through that reporting? Parker: Sure. So the first way we heard about this competition, which was not public, was almost inadvertently. We were speaking with a Cabinet secretary who said that there was an event in New York that they had kind of wanted to attend, but had declined because they didn’t want to get docked points in the competition. And we were immediately like, What competition? And so it turns out that there is this unofficial travel competition in the Trump White House. It’s overseen by a woman named Meghan Bauer, who basically coordinates with all of the Cabinet secretaries, officially running between Memorial Day and Labor Day. And basically the goal is to encourage Cabinet officials, Cabinet secretaries to travel the country, particularly to swing districts or swing states that are competitive in the midterms. And each time they go to one of these areas, they get a point. And what this Cabinet official was worried about was losing points, although the official was mistaken. When we began reporting, many officials at the White House told us, Nobody ever loses points; you only accrue points . And they even said, Look, if someone is heading to New York to, say, do a hit on CNN, to talk about Trump’s policies, that still would count as a point . Harris: We can talk about it in point systems, but we should also think of it in terms of the law, right? Like, is this a Hatch Act violation? Parker: So, no, not inherently, but it brings Cabinet officials potentially quite close to the line, and it’s something they need to be careful of. So just to put it in a little historical perspective, this general thing of wanting your top officials, your Cabinet officials, out in the country selling the president’s policies, especially in the run-up to a midterm election, is incredibly common. [George W.] Bush did it; [Barack] Obama did it; [Joe] Biden did it. And Biden, I remember, the most in-demand Cabinet official at the time, when he was president in the run-up to the midterms, was Pete Buttigieg. So Cabinet officials can go and they can talk about—especially if it’s related to their jobs, an agriculture secretary, for instance, or let’s just take Pete Buttigieg for an example. Pete Buttigieg could travel the country and talk about how this stimulus package that Biden and Democrats helped to pass had brought a bridge to your district, had brought new roads to your state, was responsible for huge construction projects over here that had created jobs. That’s all totally fine and not a Hatch Act violation. If it becomes more overtly political—showing up in a district at a campaign stop with, say, a Senate candidate and just saying, Hey, vote for Ken Paxton in Texas —that is where you get into problems. And the Trump officials, some of them have gotten into problems. Harris: Tom, how do you process the sort of flood, the stream of controversy, that comes from the administration? Nichols: Well, I actually am intimately familiar with the Hatch Act because people filed complaints against me constantly when I was a federal employee, before I came to The Atlantic . I was a professor at the Naval War College, which meant I was a Defense Department employee, but I wrote articles and I wrote op-eds and I spoke my mind. And I always finish with, These are my personal views, speaking as an American citizen, et cetera, et cetera . So I think Ashley’s description of, boy, right up to the line, is a great way to think of it. And the larger point, I think, is that, Adam, like you asked: Why does this happen? How do we cope with this flood? And I think that the flood is the point. The fire hose is the point, because at some point, you just sort of throw up your hands and say, Which of these, you know, 9 million things? It used to be that, even in the first Trump term, somebody getting hit with a Hatch Act violation was a big deal. I mean, it made the news. Kellyanne Conway, there were couple of other— Parker: Yeah, I remember the Kellyanne Conway one. And it stood out, right? Nichols: Yeah, right. Because it was rare. And because it was so obvious. And I think it’s part of that whole fire-hosing strategy, where you just sit back and say, Okay, fine. I give up, because tomorrow there will be something else . And then the Hatch Act will seem relatively minor by comparison. Parker: I was thinking about this as I was biking into work today, which is, if you even just look at today’s news, Hatch Act violations are comparatively quaint, right? I mean, I’m biking in, I see that ProPublica has reported that a Russian oligarch who’s very close to [Russian President Vladimir] Putin bankrolled Donald Trump Jr.’s intimate wedding a few months ago. And amid all these warnings that AI is going to kill us in a doomsday scenario, President Trump came out and said, We’re not slowing down; there’s no regulations . So if a Cabinet official says, Hey, vote for this Republican congressman , in the panoply of things that watchdog groups are worrying about, it’s not top of the list, to be frank. Nichols: I know the broken-windows theory of crime has been more or less discredited, but there is a kind of feeling of this of, It starts with the Hatch Act . The Hatch Act is like turnstile jumping in the subway, but enough people do it enough times and pretty soon, you know, it’s people shooting at each other in the streets and robbing banks. And it kind of feels that way now. There are no guardrails. I mean, the story that Ashley just mentioned, about Don Jr.’s wedding. Again, if you were a federal employee, if you even talked to a Russian, that was paperwork right there. I could not imagine saying, Oh yeah, and by the way, he paid for my wedding . But we’ve just kind of gotten used to it. Harris: Republicans gathered in Dallas, Texas, last week for a sort of unusual midterm convention. What did we learn about where Republicans are right now, if anything, coming out of that convention? Nichols: We learned that the party belongs to Donald Trump and that thousands of people will repeat every word he says if he tells them to. That, I think, tells you everything you need to know—about the party, not about the election, but about the party. Parker: I think that’s about right, because a lot of Republicans did not think this was a good use of time or money. If you’re actually focused on winning the midterms, they wanted to be campaigning in their districts, in their states—let alone for some of them, depending on the district or the state, aligning themselves with a president who’s quite unpopular and whose policies are quite unpopular. But nonetheless, you still saw a number of them travel to Dallas despite not really wanting to, because as Tom said, Trump is the leader of this party and he demanded a midterm convention, so he got one. Harris: I was, as I was watching it go on, thinking about what was driving the news as we were heading into the convention, which was this sort of burgeoning trade war with Canada. Trump himself mentioned Canada briefly during the convention, saying— Donald Trump: Canada very much wants to make a deal. They’re dying to make a deal. Harris: Tom, that’s all well and good, but the reality is that the president has chosen to squabble with one of America’s closest allies. Where do things stand now between the U.S. and Canada? And is there any sense of a thawing? Or do you think things are continuing to heat up? Nichols: Well, first, let’s always point out that the president’s default response to any controversy is that Country X is desperate to make a deal . It’s literally Donald Trump’s Mad Lib—one of the Mad Lib sentences. You know, What do you think about the controversy with Country X? The answer is always, Controversy will be over soon. Country X is begging to make a deal. They’re calling me every day , whether it’s Canada, Iran, the Houthis, you name it. I think the Canadians have simply decided they’ve had enough of this nonsense. They are no longer partners; they are adversaries in the economic space. But I think that the Canadians have said, Fine . A majority of the Canadians don’t want to pay for this Trump–Carney tariff war, but they support Carney standing up to Trump. And so my guess is this is not retrievable until Trump is gone from office, which is a real tragedy, even if Trump backs down from the tariffs, which he almost certainly is going to do sooner rather than later, I think. Harris: Yeah. And as you mentioned, right, Carney’s approval rating is quite high. Ashley, how has he been responding to the president, and how has the back-and-forth been going in recent days? Parker: Well, I sort of understand Carney in his response going back to a speech he gave much earlier this year at Davos, where he basically said, The world order as we— I’m paraphrasing here— the world order as we know it is over. And all of these sort of smaller countries have always supplicated themselves to the United States for protection or for deals or for various reasons, and that’s no longer a good strategy for us . And so I think Carney’s response in this trade war is him sort of acting on those principles he laid out at Davos. And one thing that was so striking to me when you look at the back-and-forth—and it looks like both sides had issues; it’s hard to point specifically to which side blew up the most recent deal—but one thing that comes through is Trump has talked about wanting Canada to be a 51st state, and that mainly seems to be trolling, except not entirely; there’s always a kernel of truth with everything Trump does. But in these negotiations, it feels like the American side has sort of internalized the idea that Canada is less a sovereign nation and more a 51st state. And when you look at the terms that Canada objected to, it was stuff the United States negotiators demanded, which would be reasonable if Canada was a state, but is not reasonable if Canada is a sovereign nation and an ally to our north. And it feels like that’s where things fell apart. Harris: Tom, actually in your piece the other day, you talked about the way that the president doesn’t view other nations as sovereign nations. There’s just this idea that he can’t go in and extract things in the way that he would if it were just a part of something that he already owned. Can you sort of flesh out that idea a little bit? Nichols: Well, I mean, not to psychoanalyze the president from a distance, but I think most people would agree the president’s a pretty narcissistic guy. He’s got to put his name on everything. He builds monuments to himself. Every sentence begins with I . And people like that don’t think of other people as real people; they think of them as players on the stage that surrounds them. And I think that’s very clear with Donald Trump. This convention, going back to the convention we were mentioning, you know, he doesn’t really think of other people trying to win elections, and he doesn’t care. They’re supposed to come to his big party and wear a hat and bring noisemakers and that’s it. And that’s the extent of his interest. And I think that’s how he is with foreign countries, that he says they’re all kind of wholly or partially owned subsidiaries of Donald Trump Incorporated . He doesn’t think of them as real places with unique cultures or particular interests led by human beings who may not actually see the world the way he does or care about his interests as much as he cares about his interests. And that’s partly why you always get these kind of stock answers of They’re gonna make a deal, because of course everybody makes a deal, because that’s what I want. And they’re gonna do what I tell them to do, because of course, all my life, everyone has done what I tell them to do . It flummoxes him completely when a foreign nation says, We’re not going to do that . And one of the reasons—you know, I don’t want to extend this analogy by Canada too far—but I think that’s one of the reasons he’s having such a hard time with the war of choice he began in Iran. He just can’t imagine that—he says, I demand that you do X, Y, and Z . And the Iranians say, No and here’s a bunch of missiles and drones as part of that answer . And I think he totally unravels him, because he’s just never had to deal with that. And I think when Mark Carney, you know, as Ashley was saying, Who is this uppity governor, to speak to the president in this way? , instead of the leader of a sovereign nation and place that’s part of NATO and has real interests in the world—one of our second or third biggest trading partners. He cannot internalize that. It doesn’t make it—it’s not like he rejects the idea. It’s like he can’t grasp the idea. Parker: And just to briefly follow on Tom, I mean, Trump has such legitimate faith and confidence in himself as a dealmaker that he really can’t fathom that. You may recall that when he was campaigning, he said, On day one, the war between Russia and Ukraine will end , which is a sort of promise presidents make— day one signals it’s a priority. But in talking to Trump’s aides, they’re like, No, no; he actually thought that . Like, he actually thought that he was such a good dealmaker, it would end. And obviously it hasn’t. Harris: When we come back, we talk about the danger of AI, and Ashley and Tom talk about what they’ll be reporting on in the week ahead. [ Music ] Harris: I wanna switch gears a little bit, speaking of the idea of things that people can and cannot control. Over the last several days, CEOs of leading AI companies have been sounding the alarm, really in a lot of the same ways that Bill Gates, when he was on the show with Hanna [Rosin] not that long ago, was talking about the growing risks of artificial intelligence and the products and the ways that people are using those products. Trump doesn’t appear to be heeding those concerns and has responded that the U.S. has to, quote, “ win AI. ” What is your reaction to this, to all of this? Nichols: That’s a classic Trump answer. You know, We have to win AI . That’s the president’s way of saying, I didn’t understand the question. I don’t really know what this is, and so we just have to win it. Because that’s a good kind of standard. You could have filled in anything: What do you think about the, you know, international chocolate-milk market? Well, we have to win that. Parker: Yeah, is winning AI , we die first? Nichols: Yeah. ( Laughs. ) What does that mean? Parker: I will confess, I don’t fully understand all of the intricacies of AI either, but from what I do understand, to be somewhat fair to Trump, or to anyone, is that this is just fundamentally incredibly complex. And, you know, lawmakers, one problem you have is if you’ve ever watched these members of Congress—which is basically a gerontocracy—try to get to the bottom of Snapchat or Instagram or social media with teens, right, it’s like they’re speaking a foreign language. And those are table stakes, right? AI is a million times more complicated than posting a problematic video on YouTube or Instagram. So first of all, a lot of the people in the United States responsible for possibly regulating this are like me, which is terrifying—can’t begin to possibly understand the nuances or the complexities. And the second thing is, even if the United States is willing to regulate, the question is you would sort of need a mutually-assured-destruction pact with China and with other countries. This is a sort of globalized problem. Nichols: I understand the intricacies very well because I have seen all the Terminator movies. And I know that Skynet is going to become self-aware at some point, and we’re going to regret it. But to go back to the president’s response, that would have been a more reassuring answer. So that’s a highly complex thing. We want to make sure that we’re handling it responsibly. And I’m fascinated to know what happened that spooked all of the top, you know, that spooked Altman and Musk and all these other guys. But I’m less of a doomer about it—even if it does scare me. But I think that the first wave of damage, if something like this gets loose, will be economic. But I still don’t know. And, you know, to go back to where we were, I don’t know what it means to win that, other than to say that we will use it to capture more efficiencies than other countries will and put more people out of work faster or something. But I think the danger of this thing is real because the people handling it—I just don’t have a sense that they are looking at this with the kind of civic responsibility that they should have. Harris: Ashley and Tom, I’m going to ask you to open your notebooks. What questions do you have going into this week? And, Ashley, I’m going to go to you first. Parker: Sure. So I’m gonna be looking at—I think actually last time I was on your podcast, we were talking about the midterms and why the bottom hasn’t fallen out for the Republicans yet. And, you know, that that was August, but things really kick off after Labor Day. There’s October surprises; voters tune in. I mean, one thing that was fascinating is I talked to someone who does focus groups with swing-state voters who said, You hold up a picture of the Senate candidate in a state, and half the voters don’t even know who he or she is . So I’m still gonna be asking those similar midterm questions, but at a time when everyone is tuning in and ads land harder; mistakes, gaffs land harder; trying to see where this heads in November. Harris: And the Republicans are starting to put more of their money into their advertising now. They’re sort of using that war chest we were talking about the last time. Parker: Yeah, because again, part of this is: They would have liked to have used it earlier. Trump has a lot of money; his groups have a lot of money. But he had to kind of release it. And even if they didn’t spend it, they wanted to get those TV reservations up early because you can get a cheaper rate if you book early. But the other reason you spend now is because this is when people are paying attention. And Michael Scherer and I spoke to Trump’s pollster Tony Fabrizio, who said at the time when we spoke, he said, Look, yeah, things are bad for the Republicans, but that’s because we haven’t turned to the Democrats yet . The Democrats have a horrible brand, and you should expect to see a ton of contrast ads because elections, as Biden always says, and as everyone understands, They’re a choice . Nichols: Ashley mentioned, or Adam, I think you mentioned October surprises. And I’m looking for one because when Trump—it gets panicky. I think one of the things I saw at the convention was that he felt very ebullient and energized, but also there was a lot of fear there. He clearly is deeply worried. And when he gets like that, you’re gonna get a surprise of some kind. He’s gonna. And it’s making me wonder what kind of thing will pop. So I guess I’m worried politically about a black-swan event, where he just does something to change the discussion. The other thing I’m watching, though, is that both in Russia and Iran, these situations are not going away. They are aware that there’s an election impending. And I have to say I don’t know why this is, but late September, early October is always a very fertile time for an international crisis. And I’m concerned that that crisis could erupt either in the Pacific, in Russia, or in Iran, because they’re not on our timetable. They’re not gonna do things on Donald Trump’s timetable or do things based on his interests. And I think all of those places that we’ve stopped watching temporarily because of so much going on at home are percolating, and I’m concerned about what happens next in each of those three, especially in the Ukraine war and in Iran. Harris: Well, Ashley, Tom, thank you so much for joining me today and helping me sift through the news of the week. Parker: Thank you for having us. Nichols: Thanks, Adam. Harris: That’s all for today’s show. This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Mike Pesoli and edited by Hadley Robinson. It has original music by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. If you like what you saw here, new episodes of Radio Atlantic drop every Monday and Thursday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube page, on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work and the work of my colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Until next time, I’m Adam Harris.

items.title: Droits d’auteur au Burkina Faso : Le BBDA va distribuer plus de 1,5 milliard de F CFA pour la session d’août 2026
items.description: Le Bureau burkinabè du droit d’auteur (BBDA) a annoncé, ce 14 septembre 2026, les montants de la répartition des droits d’auteur au titre du mois d’août. Les sommes attribuées aux bénéficiaires varient de 3 900 FCFA à près de 12 millions de FCFA. Au total, 32 852 bénéficiaires , dont 16 346 membres du BBDA , sont concernés par cette opération. Après application des différents prélèvements, notamment les frais de gestion, le fonds de promotion culturelle et les œuvres sociales, le montant net affecté à la répartition s’établit à 1 522 424 728 FCFA . Une hausse de 11,61 % en un an La répartition des droits, pour le directeur général du BBDA, Zita Daniel Bonzi, ne constitue pas une simple opération financière. Elle traduit la reconnaissance de la valeur du travail des créateurs et des autres titulaires de droits. « Répartir les droits, ce n’est donc pas simplement procéder à une opération comptable » , a-t-il confié. Les redevances prises en compte pour cette opération s’élèvent à 2 395 288 540,44 FCFA . Après les retenues statutaires, le montant net affecté à la répartition est de 1 522 424 728 FCFA . Par rapport à l’exercice précédent, le montant net réparti progresse de 11,61 % , des dires du directeur général, soit une hausse de 158 384 206 FCFA . Le nombre de membres bénéficiaires passe également de 16 077 en août 2025 à 16 346 en août 2026 , soit une progression de 1,67 % . Plusieurs catégories de droits concernées Cette hausse globale ne signifie toutefois pas une augmentation automatique des droits perçus par chaque bénéficiaire, a expliqué Daniel Bonzi. Les montants individuels tiennent notamment compte du nombre de membres et du volume des œuvres pris en considération lors des opérations de répartition. La répartition porte sur plusieurs catégories de droits. Il s’agit notamment des droits de reproduction mécanique issus des redevances collectées auprès des éditeurs de phonogrammes et de vidéogrammes, ainsi que des droits de reproduction par reprographie, dont bénéficie notamment une partie de la presse écrite. S’y ajoutent la rémunération équitable au titre des droits voisins, la rémunération pour copie privée et les droits provenant de l’étranger. Pour le BBDA, cette diversité des sources nécessite une adaptation continue des mécanismes de collecte, de documentation, de traitement et de répartition. 550 747 105 FCFA de droits en instance L’opération comprend également des droits en instance au titre des exercices antérieurs. Leur montant s’élève à 550 747 105 FCFA . Ces sommes concernent les exercices 2022, 2023, 2024 et 2025 , ainsi que les répartitions de février et mai 2026 . Ces droits seront progressivement mis en paiement. La direction générale entend, dans le même temps, poursuivre l’amélioration de la collecte des redevances et renforcer l’identification ainsi que la documentation des œuvres. L’accélération des opérations de répartition et la réduction des droits en instance figurent également parmi les priorités annoncées. Le BBDA prévoit aussi de poursuivre la modernisation de ses mécanismes de paiement et la sensibilisation des utilisateurs d’œuvres sur leurs obligations en matière de droits d’auteur et de droits voisins. Le paiement débute mardi Le paiement des droits débutera le mardi 15 septembre 2026 à partir de 8 heures . Plusieurs modes de paiement sont prévus : virements bancaires, paiements électroniques par Orange Money et paiements par chèque pour tout montant supérieur ou égal à 100 000 FCFA . Les paiements en espèces sont également prévus dans les sites concernés. Le paiement électronique sera toutefois privilégié afin de réduire les contraintes liées aux déplacements et de renforcer la sécurisation des opérations. Le directeur général du BBDA souligne l’objectif poursuivi par cette diversification. « Cette diversification des modes de paiement répond à un objectif simple. raccrocher le paiement au bénéficiaire, réduire les contraintes liées au déplacement et sécuriser davantage les opérations financières », a-t-il ajouté. À travers ces différentes mesures, le BBDA entend renforcer l’efficacité de la collecte, du traitement et de la redistribution des droits au profit des titulaires. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article Droits d'auteur au Burkina Faso : Le BBDA va distribuer plus de 1,5 milliard de F CFA pour la session d'août 2026 est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Modernisation de l’Administration : cap sur des services publics plus efficaces et proches du Peuple
items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a présidé, ce lundi 14 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la session ordinaire du Conseil national de la modernisation de l’Administration et de la bonne gouvernance (CN-MABG). Les travaux ont permis d’évaluer les performances de l’Administration publique, d’identifier les insuffisances persistantes et de définir les orientations pour l’année 2027. À l’ouverture de la session, le Chef du Gouvernement a rappelé que la modernisation de l’Administration publique constitue un enjeu de souveraineté, de dignité et d’efficacité de l’action publique. Elle ne saurait, selon lui, se limiter à des réformes techniques ou à la dématérialisation des procédures. « Notre ambition doit être claire : faire de l’Administration publique un véritable instrument de souveraineté et de transformation du Burkina Faso », a-t-il déclaré. Le Premier ministre a ainsi appelé à un changement profond des pratiques, des méthodes de travail et du rapport de l’Administration au Peuple. L’objectif est de bâtir une Administration disciplinée, intègre, compétente, performante, innovante et redevable, capable de produire des résultats et de rendre compte de l’utilisation des ressources publiques. La performance globale de l’Administration au titre de l’année 2025, établie à 85,38 %, témoigne, selon le Chef du Gouvernement, d’une dynamique appréciable. Tout en félicitant les agents publics ayant contribué à ce résultat, il les a invités à se garder de toute autosatisfaction. « La performance n’est pas une fin en soi : elle est une exigence permanente », a-t-il souligné, insistant sur la nécessité de traduire les résultats administratifs en améliorations concrètes dans la vie des populations. Les travaux ont également permis d’examiner les principales insuffisances qui affectent encore le fonctionnement de l’Administration. Elles concernent notamment la faible couverture de l’évaluation de certaines institutions, l’appropriation insuffisante des outils de gouvernance, les contraintes liées aux ressources humaines et aux infrastructures, les difficultés des systèmes d’information ainsi que l’authenticité de certains documents produits dans le cadre de la commande publique. L’appropriation des plateformes de services numériques par les citoyens figure également parmi les défis identifiés. À ce sujet, le Premier ministre a appelé à une transformation numérique inclusive, adaptée aux réalités nationales et qui ne crée pas de nouvelles formes d’exclusion. Il a notamment souhaité que les langues nationales trouvent progressivement leur place dans les systèmes d’information et les services numériques. Au cours de la session, les participants ont examiné trois principaux documents : le rapport annuel de mise en œuvre de la Stratégie nationale de modernisation de l’Administration publique, le rapport sur l’état de la gouvernance au Burkina Faso et le rapport global sur la performance des structures de l’Administration publique, tous au titre de l’année 2025. Ils ont également analysé les résultats des évaluations des stratégies nationales relatives à la déconcentration administrative, à la modernisation de l’Administration publique et à la promotion de la bonne gouvernance. À la clôture des travaux, le Premier ministre a engagé les responsables concernés à transformer les recommandations adoptées en actions concrètes, assorties de responsabilités clairement définies et de mécanismes rigoureux de suivi. Il a précisé que les insuffisances relevées ne remettent pas en cause les performances enregistrées, mais constituent des défis prioritaires auxquels des réponses doivent être apportées. Les orientations définies pour 2027 devront notamment permettre à l’Administration d’accompagner la reconquête du territoire et le retour effectif de l’État auprès des populations. « Là où nos Forces combattantes reconquièrent des espaces, notre Administration doit être prête à rétablir durablement la présence et l’autorité de l’État », a affirmé le Chef du Gouvernement. Pour Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, le rétablissement de la sécurité doit s’accompagner du retour de services publics adaptés aux besoins des populations, notamment dans les domaines de l’éducation, de la santé, de l’état civil, de la justice, de l’action sociale et de l’administration territoriale. Le Premier ministre a enfin appelé chaque ministère, institution, structure et agent public à prendre sa part dans la refondation de l’Administration, sous le sceau de la primauté de l’intérêt général. Il a chargé le ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, à travers le Secrétariat permanent de la modernisation de l’Administration et de la bonne gouvernance, d’assurer un suivi rigoureux de la mise en œuvre des conclusions et orientations issues de la session. items.title: Droits d’auteur au Burkina Faso : Plus de 2 milliards de FCFA mis en paiement par le BBDA pour la session d’août 2026
items.description: Réuni en conférence de presse le lundi 14 septembre 2026, le Bureau Burkinabè du Droit d’Auteur (BBDA) a présenté les résultats et les modalités de paiement relatifs à la répartition des droits du mois d’août 2026. Portée par un montant net de 1 522 424 728 FCFA, en progression de 11,61 % par rapport à l'année précédente, cette opération intègre également 550 745 105 FCFA au titre des droits en instance. Au total, plus de 2 milliards de FCFA seront versés dès ce mardi 15 septembre 2026 à 32 852 bénéficiaires, témoignant de l'engagement de l'institution en faveur de la transparence et de la valorisation du travail des créateurs. Le Bureau Burkinabè du Droit d’Auteur (BBDA) a animé une conférence de presse le lundi 14 septembre 2026 afin de faire le point sur l'opération de répartition des droits du mois d’août 2026. Dans sa déclaration liminaire, le Directeur Général du BBDA, le Camarade Zita Daniel BONZI, a souligné que cette rencontre s'inscrit dans une démarche continue de transparence et de dialogue avec les titulaires de droits et le grand public. Pour cette session, les redevances globales collectées s’élèvent à 2 395 288 544 FCFA. Après déduction des retenues statutaires, le montant net mis en répartition s’établit à 1 522 424 728 FCFA, contre 1 364 040 522 FCFA en août 2025, soit une hausse remarquable de 11,61 %. Plus de 32 000 bénéficiaires et résorption des droits en instance À cette somme nette s’ajoute une enveloppe de 550 745 105 FCFA correspondant aux droits en instance issus des exercices 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 ainsi que des sessions de février et mai 2026. L'ensemble de ces ressources porte le montant total mis en paiement à 2 027 361 636 FCFA au profit de 32 852 bénéficiaires, dont 16 346 membres affiliés au BBDA. Ces derniers perçoivent à eux seuls 1 412 867 131 FCFA, soit environ 93 % des droits nets répartis. De plus, le BBDA octroie un Droit Minimum Payable (DMP) de 3 900 FCFA aux membres concernés, ce qui représente une dotation globale de 63 749 400 FCFA. Catégories de droits et précisions sur la répartition individuelle Au cours de la rencontre, la Camarade Delphine SOMÉ/ZONGO, Directrice de la Documentation Générale et de la Répartition, a explicité les bases techniques régissant les calculs. La répartition du mois d’août englobe plusieurs catégories : les Droits de Reproduction Mécanique (provenant des éditeurs de phonogrammes et vidéogrammes), les Droits de Reproduction par Reprographie (dont une part revient à la presse écrite), la Rémunération Équitable au titre des droits voisins, la Rémunération pour Copie Privée et les droits collectés à l’étranger. Toutefois, le Directeur Général a rappelé que la hausse de la masse globale répartie ne garantit pas automatiquement une augmentation des gains individuels, chaque part dépendant directement du degré d'exploitation effective des œuvres. Démarrage effectif des paiements et canaux de règlement Le lancement officiel des règlements est fixé au mardi 15 septembre 2026. Afin d'assurer un processus fluide et sécurisé, le BBDA diversifie ses modes de paiement : virements bancaires, règlements par paiement mobile ( mobile money ), chèques pour les sommes égales ou supérieures à 100 000 FCFA, et paiements en espèces disponibles aux guichets de Ouagadougou et de Bobo-Dioulasso. items.title: Nouna : une soirée d’horreur au secteur 4, deux morts et un homme maîtrisé après une série d’agressions.
items.description: Un marchand de bétail aurait tué son épouse et son ami, incendié des engins et semé la panique jusque dans une mosquée. Un dozo, intervenu avec courage, aurait contribué à éviter un bilan plus lourd. Une tragédie d’une rare violence a frappé le secteur 4 de Nouna dans la soirée du dimanche 13 septembre 2026. Selon plusieurs témoignages recueillis, un homme identifié comme Soré Sayouba, âgé de plus de 40 ans, polygame et père de six enfants, aurait commis une série d’actes meurtriers avant d’être maîtrisé par un brave dozo. Originaire de Dara et marchand de bétail, l’intéressé aurait d’abord agressé sa troisième épouse, Afousétou Soré, étudiante et future élève infirmière. Âgée de 26 ans, mariée et mère d’une fillette de quatre ans, Afousétou est étudiante à l’Université Nazi Boni de Dédougou, où elle a validé sa deuxième année en économie et mathématiques avec une moyenne de 14/20. D’après les témoignages, il l’aurait poursuivie avant de l’atteindre à son domicile et de l’égorger sur son lit. Un ami attiré sur les lieux, puis tué. Selon les témoignages recueillis, Daouda Zallé a alors été agressé à son tour. Il aurait été poignardé à plusieurs reprises, puis son corps a été jeté dans le feu des engins incendiés. Un autre ami, nommé Souley, a également été appelé par le mis en cause. À son arrivée, il aurait découvert ce dernier armé d’une machette et d’une daba. « Il m’a dit qu’il avait tué sa femme. Il tenait une machette et une daba avant de se jeter sur moi. Je me suis sauvé dans un champ de maïs », a-t-il témoigné tout en se lâchant avec une voix nouée » C'est une grande chance pour moi ». Le courage d’un dozo pour éviter un bilan plus lourd C’est dans ce contexte qu’un dozo présenté comme Kassoum Dama, originaire du village de Sanso, serait intervenu. Il aurait réussi à maîtriser et à ligoter le mis en cause. Selon son témoignage, l’homme lui aurait alors demandé de l’achever. « Lorsque j’ai pu le ligoter, il m’a dit de le terminer pour de bon. » Toujours selon ce témoignage, le mis en cause aurait évoqué, dans un discours jugé incohérent, un projet visant à éliminer quatre personnes avant de se donner lui-même la mort. L’intervention de Kassoum Dama aurait ainsi permis de mettre fin à la série d’agressions et, potentiellement, d’éviter d’autres victimes. Une tentative de suicide après les faits Après ces événements, Soré Sayouba aurait tenté de se suicider en se blessant avec sa machette et sa pioche. Il aurait subi des blessures à la gorge et à la tête. Des proches rapportent qu’il aurait récemment répudié sa troisième épouse, allant jusqu’à incendier ses effets personnels. Ils affirment toutefois n’avoir constaté aucun signe manifeste de démence avant le drame : l’homme fréquentait ses amis et échangeait normalement avec son entourage. Un autre témoignage, recueilli au cimetière municipal, évoque un possible traumatisme ancien. Selon un jeune homme présent sur les lieux, l’intéressé aurait échappé, il y a longtemps, à une attaque terroriste le jour du marché hebdomadaire de Bomborokuy où il a été pour l'achat du bétail, un événement qui lui aurait causé un choc psychologique. Il aurait eu du mal à retrouver son domicile à Nouna après l'attaque. Ce récit, qui n’a pas été confirmé par une source médicale ou officielle, ne permet pas, à lui seul, d’établir un lien avec les actes commis dimanche. Une ville sous le choc Ce lundi 14 septembre 2026, l’émotion était vive à la morgue, au cimetière municipal et dans les différentes familles des victimes. La douleur des proches se mêlait à l’incompréhension face à une violence aussi soudaine. Au-delà de l’horreur des faits, ce drame soulève de nombreuses interrogations sur les circonstances ayant conduit à cette explosion de violence. Seule une enquête rigoureuse, appuyée au besoin par une expertise médicale et psychologique, permettra d’établir les faits, les responsabilités et les éventuels facteurs explicatifs. En attendant le mis en cause a été arrêté et transmis aux forces de sécurité. Aux dernières nouvelles ,il a subi des soins intensifs au CMA de Nouna et son pronostic vital n'est pas engagé. Quant aux deux victimes, elles ont été inhumées dans la matinée du lundi au cimetière municipal de Nouna. Source: Madi Sidparaadye Kébré Burkinaweb. net L’article Nouna : une soirée d’horreur au secteur 4, deux morts et un homme maîtrisé après une série d’agressions. est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Production de données statistiques : le Burkina 1er en Open data en Afrique de l’Ouest
items.description: L’Institut national de la statistique et de la démographie a tenu sa première session ordinaire du conseil national de la statistique de l’année, le 11 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, sur le thème : « Les statistiques publiques au service de la mise en œuvre du suivi-évaluation et de la redevabilité du Plan de relance 2026-2030 ». L’Institut national de la statistique et de la démographie (INSD) veut renforcer le rôle des statistiques publiques dans la conduite des politiques de développement. C’est dans cette perspective que s’est tenue le vendredi 11 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la première session ordinaire de l’année du Conseil national de la statistique (CNS). Placée sur le thème : « Les statistiques publiques au service de la mise en œuvre du suivi-évaluation et de la redevabilité du Plan de relance 2026-2030 », la rencontre a réuni des représentants des ministères, ainsi que les différents acteurs du système statistique national. Cette première session ordinaire de l’année a permis d’examiner le rapport statistique national 2025 et de valider le projet de Programme statistique national 2027. La rencontre a été l’occasion de mettre en avant la volonté du Burkina Faso de disposer de données produites et maitrisées au niveau national. Le président du CNS est le ministre de l’Economie et des Finances. Il a été représenté à cette session par le Secrétaire général (SG) du département Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama. Selon lui, dans la mise en œuvre du 5e Schéma directeur de la statistique (SDS)2026-2030 dont le coût global est estimé à 96,689 milliards F CFA, l’enjeu est de parvenir à un système statistique moderne, performant et fiable. L’activité statistique en progression malgré les défis Il a présenté cette orientation comme un choix de souveraineté, permettant au pays de produire lui-même les informations nécessaires à la compréhension de ses réalités et à l’orientation de ses politiques publiques. Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama a souligné que malgré un contexte sécuritaire difficile, les activités statistiques ont enregistré une progression en 2025. « Le taux d’exécution est passé de 65,6 % en 2024 à 67,8 % en 2025 », a-t-il révélé. Un projet de Programme statistique 2027 évalué à 10,6 milliards F CFA Cette performance, a poursuivi le SG du ministère en charge de l’économie, s’accompagne également d’une reconnaissance internationale dans le domaine de l’open data. En effet, le Burkina Faso s’est classé premier en Afrique de l’Ouest et deuxième à l’échelle du continent dans le classement mondial de l’open data, avec un score de 77 points sur 100, a-t-il indiqué. « Ces résultats reflètent un engagement collectif dont je remercie l’ensemble des acteurs du système statistique national », a-t-il clamé. Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama a invité l’ensemble des acteurs à maintenir leurs efforts, poursuivre l’innovation dans la production et l’utilisation des données, et faire des statistiques un véritable outil d’aide à la décision et un levier du développement durable. Face à l’évolution des besoins en matière d’information statistique, l’INSD entend également s’appuyer sur les nouvelles technologies pour moderniser ses méthodes de travail. Le directeur général de l’INSD, Toubou Ripama, a énuméré quelques innovations. Il s’agit de la création de l’observatoire national d’innovation statistique, du déploiement d’un centre d’appel dédié aux enquêtes par téléphone, de la prise en compte de l’intelligence artificielle, de la digitalisation des outils de collecte, ainsi que de la modernisation des plateformes de diffusion des donnés. Pour Toubou Ripama, ces différentes actions traduisent la volonté de l’INSD de construire un système statistique davantage adapté aux réalités et aux besoins futurs du Burkina. Le projet de Programme statistique national 2027, soumis à l’examen du CNS, est évalué à 10,6 milliards F CFA. L’Etat burkinabè va prendre en charge 52,7 % du financement selon le directeur général de l’INSD. « Cela traduit l’appropriation nationale croissante de notre système, tout en rappelant la nécessité de poursuivre la mobilisation des ressources pérennes et de partenariats diversifiés », a-t-il indiqué. items.title: FG targets $100bn tourism, creative economy with ‘Ember To Remember 2026’ national season
items.description: By Benjamin Njoku The Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy has reaffirmed its commitment to partner with state governments, investors, creative entrepreneurs, technology platforms, hospitality businesses and other stakeholders to build an ecosystem that can unlock Nigeria’s $100 billion tourism and creative economy potential. Speaking at the official flag-off of “Ember to Remember 2026” and the unveiling of the national calendar in Lagos on Monday, Minister Hannatu Musa Musawa said the ministry is working toward a tourism and creative economy that contributes meaningfully to Nigeria’s GDP all year round. According to her, the goal is an economy that creates opportunities for young Nigerians, attracts investment, strengthens local businesses, and projects Nigeria positively to the world. “Ember to Remember 2026” is a 100-day national tourism season running from September to December. Musawa said it aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s economic vision to expand Nigeria’s economic base, unlock new growth sectors, create jobs, and position the private sector as a key driver of national development. “Our ambition must, however, go beyond December. It requires deliberate planning, collaboration, investment and execution to drive this initiative,” she said. “The $100 billion opportunity will not be created by one ministry, one company or one event. It will be created by an ecosystem. And that ecosystem is represented in this room today. So I challenge every organisation here to ask: What role can we play in building Nigeria’s next major economic growth sector? “Let this conference mark the beginning of a stronger partnership between government and the private sector. Let us make Ember to Remember a platform that connects our destinations, our events, our businesses and our people to a much larger national and global market “And most importantly, let us populate the calendar, promote Nigeria and convert our celebrations into sustainable economic value. Nigeria has the culture. Nigeria has the creativity. Nigeria has the people. Nigeria has the market. Now, we must build the economy around it,”_ Musawa said. The Minister tasked the private sector to lead the transformation, while government provides the enabling environment through policy, infrastructure, security, destination development and ease of movement. She also commended Mrs. Ifeoma Chukwu, CEO of MyCityApp, for her commitment, assuring all partners of the ministry’s support. “This is precisely the kind of partnership we must encourage, where government provides the enabling environment while innovative Nigerians create platforms, products and opportunities that move our economy forward. This initiative is about moving beyond the traditional concept of a festive season. It is about deliberately organising, packaging, promoting and monetising one of the most economically active periods in our national calendar,” she added. Also speaking, Ifeoma Chukwu said the essence of the initiative is to promote Nigeria’s cultural, tourism and creative offerings from September to December. The calendar is expected to help Nigerians, members of the diaspora and international visitors discover events and experiences across Nigeria’s 36 states and the FCT. “MyCityApp is a digital city and tourism platform connecting people to Nigeria’s events, destinations, hospitality, culture and experiences. Nigeria is rich in culture with one of the most vibrant creative industries in the world. The opportunity is to turn every visitor’s experience into economic value. That is how celebration becomes commerce. And tourism becomes an economy,” Chukwu said. In attendance were Mr. Babajide Olusola Sanwo Olu, Executive Governor of Lagos State, who was represented by Honorable Toke Benson-Awoyink, the Lagos State Commissioner for Tourism, Arts and Culture, His excellency Dr, Peter Ndubisi Mbah, Governor of Enugu State,also represented by Honorable Barrister Ugochi Madueke, the Enugu State Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, His excellency Alhaji Mohammed Idris Malagi, the Honorable Minister of Information and National Orientation of Nigeria, represented by Dr. Olalekan Fadolapo, Director General of the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) among other stakeholders. items.title: Burkina Faso: un bébé d’environ un mois abandonné avec sa layette dans le quartier Saonré de Ouagadougou
items.description: Un bébé de sexe féminin, âgé d’environ un mois, a été abandonné avec sa layette, ce lundi 14 septembre 2026 à l’aube, près d’un kiosque au quartier Saonré de Ouagadougou. Découvert vers 6 h, le nourrisson était en bonne santé et dormait toujours malgré l’attroupement, a confié Annick Palm/Bakyono, sage-femme du CSPS de Tingindalgué présente sur les lieux au journaliste de l’AIB sur place. Les habitants du quartier Saonré de Ouagadougou se sont réveillés ce lundi par la découverte d’un bébé de sexe féminin âgé d’environ un mois abandonné par sa mère avec toute sa layette. Entre émotions, indignations, accusations et interrogations certains se sont manifestés volontairement pour adopter le nourrisson. L’entrepreneur en BTP, Mansour Zongo, ayant déjà deux femmes et quatre enfants, a expliqué qu’une vie ne peut être achetée et pour aucune raison, un enfant ne doit être abandonné. De ce fait, il a ajouté qu’il dispose des moyens nécessaires pour adopter le bébé et bien s’occuper de lui. Il appelle à la responsabilité des hommes pour prévenir de telles situations et surtout invite les filles à adopter de bonnes habitudes afin de préserver la vie d’enfants innocents. Pour Annick Palm/Bakyono, a invité les personnes intéressées à l’adoption du bébé à se référer aux services du ministère en charge de la Famille pour les éventuelles procédures. Au moment où le journaliste de l’AIB quittait les lieux, les sapeurs-pompiers, la sage-femme ainsi que les riverains attendaient la police pour le constat, avant toute prise en charge sanitaire et d’éventuelles procédures administratives. items.title: Trump’s See-No-Evil AI Policy
items.description: N ot long ago , most of Washington was scrambling to be as friendly as possible to the rise of artificial intelligence. Lawmakers from both parties saw a chance to bolster the nation’s economy—and their campaign coffers. But rarely has public opinion flipped so quickly and so thoroughly as it has on AI in recent months. While AI was making some tech leaders unfathomably rich, many Americans in states both red and blue grew alarmed by the proliferation of loud, electricity-guzzling data centers, convinced that AI would first make life more expensive and then, for good measure, eliminate their job. In the past few days, some of the top voices in the AI industry have gone further , warning that unless development of the technology is slowed, and slowed soon, all of humanity could be made extinct. These fears have rattled markets and galvanized a bipartisan set of leaders into calling for the government to step in. AI has now become a central issue in the midterm elections. But President Trump, who first came to power by closely reading the mood of the country and shifting his views to meet those of the electorate, seems to have his fingers in his ears, ignoring it all and continuing to embrace AI, confident that everything will be fine because he is in charge. Unless, of course, the human race ends first. Trump would seem to have a perfect opportunity to try to contain this fast-moving political conflagration: Next week, he’s set to host China’s president , Xi Jinping, at the White House. The United States and China are the world’s leaders on AI and are in a race to develop the technology. The summit could be a venue, some in the industry hope, to order a pause in development or establish international safety guidelines. But Trump, at least for now, wants no part of a slowdown. AI growth has propped up Wall Street and sectors of the American economy for the duration of his second term, and the president has made clear that he doesn’t want to do anything that could burst that bubble. “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” Trump wrote on Truth Social today, as he made half a dozen posts, each seemingly more frantic than the last. He later compared the concerns about the technology to his own impeachments, declaring that “AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX.” A s tech insiders offered warnings about the AI apocalypse, Trump was busy rallying the MAGA faithful in Texas and taking in rounds of golf in Ireland. The dire prophecies began last Tuesday, with a series of viral social-media posts by an AI researcher who said that the technology is advancing so quickly that it could bring about human extinction by the end of the decade. The threat of annihilation seemed to grab Washington’s attention as few other concerns have. By the next afternoon, after several other researchers had echoed the alarm, members of Congress were beginning to call for legislation, new agencies, hearings, and regulations to address the threat. Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont told us on Wednesday that he had sent invitations to a bipartisan set of lawmakers for a closed-door briefing with AI experts. He said that the researchers had provided a wake-up call about a technology that poses an “extraordinary danger for the human race.” That night, Trump spoke for nearly two hours at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas , but he did not mention AI once. [ Read: AI is running laps around our political system ] In the days that followed, more troubling evidence emerged. Anthropic released a report detailing the ways that individuals and nation-states have attempted to misuse its technology, including for sophisticated cyberattacks and research that could potentially support the development of biological weapons. Trump decamped to Ireland, where he spent the weekend watching a golf tournament at one of his properties. He was dismissive of the Silicon Valley warnings, emphasizing the need to defeat China in the AI race and downplaying the technology’s risks. On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote that a downshift in the pace of AI development “could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong.” Other industry leaders joined in, including OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Elon Musk , the sometimes–Trump ally. O ne of Trump’s first moves upon returning to office last year was to revoke the executive order signed by his predecessor, Joe Biden, that imposed a series of regulations on the AI industry. Trump’s focus was business growth, and he reveled in the power he had over the nation’s tech titans. Many crowded the room at his inauguration , and he has hosted AI-industry leaders such as Altman, former Oracle CEO Safra Catz, and Nvidia President Jensen Huang. Still, some of Trump’s advisers have had concerns since last year about the political impacts of the AI backlash, when figures as disparate as Sanders and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis began calling for more regulation. To head off the potential populist backlash, Trump announced the Ratepayer Protection Pledge in March, asking major developers of AI to “build, bring, or buy” resources needed for any new electricity-production and utility-infrastructure upgrades. Now the White House is working with House Speaker Mike Johnson to fast-track legislation that would put into law some of the pledge’s voluntary measures. A vote is scheduled for tomorrow. [ From the March issue: America isn’t ready for what AI will do to jobs ] People close to the administration perceive some figures, including White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, to be supportive of additional regulation of the industry, two people familiar with internal White House deliberations told us, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Others, such as Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, have advocated for as little government interference as possible, while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has demanded that Anthropic abandon ethical safeguards—such as rules against mass surveillance and autonomous lethal targeting—in its work for the Pentagon. (When Anthropic refused, Hegseth cut ties with the company.) Trump has dug in on letting AI rip. He has watched as the industry has propelled the stock market, the president’s favorite indicator of a strong economy, keeping it high even amid challenges posed by the Iran conflict, stubborn inflation, and tariffs. Trump has expressed worry to those close to him that a halt to AI expansion could send the economy into a recession, one ally told us. Some in the president’s orbit have raised suspicions about the AI executives’ warnings: Is this an attempt at market capture? (They worry that new regulations would freeze the industry and prevent would-be competitors from catching up to the industry giants.) Vice President Vance seemed to give expression to that idea by saying today that tech companies “begging the government to regulate them” feels “like a bit of a Trojan horse.” David Sacks , a co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, wondered on social media over the weekend why AI companies cannot just regulate themselves; he told tech leaders to “stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel.” (Top AI firms could work together to implement some safety standards, but antitrust law would likely prevent them from implementing any kind of reciprocal agreement to throttle the pace of development, unless Congress granted a waiver for that purpose, MacKenzie Arnold, the managing director of the Institute for Law and AI, a nonpartisan think tank, told The Atlantic .) Today, Trump called Huang while the CEO was onstage at an AI event to assure the Nvidia head that he will keep supporting the technology. [ Read: J. D. Vance’s AI doctrine ] The pleas for action have created unlikely political bedfellows. Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, a Republican, declared that “we need substantially more regulation,” while Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, a Democrat, said that Congress needs to “move at the pace of the threat.” Tomorrow, Sanders will join the Trump adviser Steve Bannon at a “Pro-Human Assembly,” an all-day gathering in Washington, D.C., focused on ensuring that humans remain in charge of AI. Despite support for regulation from both the right and the left, there is little meaningful oversight of AI that can be implemented without the president’s approval. Sanders told us that he hopes the bipartisan outrage will ultimately get Trump’s attention. “Trump’s ignorance is extremely dangerous,” he said. “He has not a clue about the dangers inherent in this technology, nor do people in his administration.” T rump is looking forward to next week’s summit with Xi, which follows a May meeting in Beijing . The U.S. president has stressed his strong relationship with the Chinese leader and has downplayed China’s efforts to thwart the United States. It seems unlikely that Trump will let AI fears fully derail the summit’s agenda. Trump has also minimized China’s chances of catching up to the U.S.—he green-lighted a sale of Nvidia chips to China late last year—even as he has played up the stakes. “Whoever wins AI wins,” he said this past weekend. But Xi may come into the meeting with a new wariness of his own. China’s top intelligence official warned yesterday that AI could pose a direct threat to the Chinese Communist Party’s hold on power by enabling sophisticated hacking and disinformation campaigns. Many in the industry hope that the summit will be an inflection point. Nate Persily, a co-director of the Stanford Law AI Initiative, told us that “if ever there was an opportunity to get some kind of consensus on AI safety, this provides that opportunity.” And Altman, in an interview over the weekend, made a clever appeal to Trump’s vanity, suggesting that if he and Xi strike some sort of deal to create AI guardrails, the president could win his long-coveted Nobel Peace Prize. Michael Scherer, Ashley Parker, Will Oremus, and Jack Rodriquez-Vars contributed reporting.

items.title: Hafia FC vs AS Douanes reprogrammé : le Hafia FC conteste la décision de la CAF et entend saisir les juridictions compétentes
items.description: Le Hafia FC refuse de laisser passer la décision de la CAF, concernant le match retour du premier tour préliminaire de la Coupe de la Confédération face à l'AS Douanes de Mauritanie. Tout en annonçant un recours devant les juridictions compétentes, le club guinéen confirme qu'il disputera la rencontre reprogrammée, attendue selon nos informations le week-end des 18, 19 ou 20 septembre. Initialement prévue le 11 septembre au stade du 28 Septembre de Conakry, la rencontre n'avait pas pu se tenir en raison de l'absence de l'AS Douanes sur le territoire guinéen. La Commission d'Organisation des Compétitions Interclubs de la CAF a depuis décidé de reprogrammer le match, en retenant un cas de force majeure. Dans un communiqué officiel, le Hafia FC affirme avoir pris connaissance de la décision de l'instance continentale, tout en indiquant qu'il la conteste. « Le Hafia Football Club conteste d'ores et déjà cette décision et entend faire valoir ses droits devant les juridictions compétentes de la CAF et, si cela s'avère nécessaire, devant le Tribunal Arbitral du Sport », écrit le club. Par cette position, le vice-champion de Guinée entend défendre ses intérêts tout en empruntant les voies réglementaires prévues par les textes de la CAF. Malgré son désaccord, le Hafia FC assure qu'il respectera les décisions relatives au calendrier de la compétition. « Dans un esprit de respect des instances et de la compétition, le Hafia FC confirme sa disponibilité à disputer la rencontre à la date qui sera retenue pour sa reprogrammation », précise le communiqué. Selon nos informations, la CAF a fixé le match retour durant le week-end des 18, 19 ou 20 septembre 2026. Le Hafia FC invite également ses supporters et l'ensemble des acteurs du football guinéen à faire preuve de retenue pendant la procédure. « Le Hafia FC appelle ses supporters, ainsi que l'ensemble de la famille du football guinéen, à la sérénité, au calme et au respect des procédures en cours. » Le communiqué s'achève sur une déclaration ferme, traduisant la volonté du club de défendre sa position : « Le Hafia Football Club entend se faire respecter ».
